newsitem.title: UK: British doctors announce first world HRT study.
newsitem.headline: British doctors announce first world HRT study.

text.p: British doctors announced on Monday they would coordinate the world's first study of the long-term effects of hormone-replacement therapy (HRT) on women.
More than 30,000 women aged 50 to 64 who have gone through the menopause will be recruited for the trial, which will compare hormone pills with placebos containing no drug.

The trial, known as the Women's International Study of Long-Duration Oestrogen After Menopause (WISDOM), will last for 20 years, with first results announced in 2012, Britain's Medical Research Council (MRC) said in a statement.
"We are optimistic that this will yield some extremely valuable answers to a host of questions about the implications of HRT for women's health," said Dr Madge Vickers of the MRC.
Menopausal women are often prescribed HRT to prevent symptoms such as osteoporosis, a thinning of the bones believed to be related to loss of oestrogen.
HRT has also been linked to a slightly higher rate of breast cancer, while at the same time offering what seems to be protection against heart disease.
